title: The store's whole run no longer swaps the Mac to a stop: the decision sets stream, and the scheduler stops a run that does not fit
request: The owner's scheduled store run (python -m dclab_rnd.store run) had run four and a half hours on an 8 GB Mac at a footprint near nine gigabytes, swapping. The owner said: stop it, run it at 01:30, then run the whole store.
spec: A whole store run finishes on an 8 GB Mac, and a run that cannot is stopped before it fills the disk, however slowly it answers an interrupt.
plan: identify the process and why it was slow
stop it, pause the six-hour schedule, schedule one run
find the stage that spikes in memory from the stack at the stop
keep only what the decision sets need
stop a run at four gigabytes of swap, escalating the signal
build every stage of the sets in its own process

decisions.decision: The scheduler stops a run at four gigabytes of swap or under two of free disk, with an interrupt, then terminate, then kill
decisions.why: an interrupt had no effect for ten minutes while the process swapped; the store writes through atomic replaces

decisions.decision: Build the sets stage by stage in separate processes when a whole run cannot fit
decisions.why: every stage fits alone; the whole run held the earlier stages' memory

change: dclab_rnd/store/sets/decisions.py (one pass keeping only wanted decisions, labels and sources; slim placements), scripts/store_scheduled.py (swap guard, stop escalation), tests/test_store_scheduled.py.

findings.defect: The decision sets held every shaped decision record as an object at once
findings.scenario: a whole store run's footprint jumped from about six hundred megabytes to over six gigabytes in one minute while building the decision sets
findings.cause: a dictionary of every record of the kind, and one whole curator choice for each of one and a half million placements
findings.fix: one pass keeping only the placed decisions, the labels and the source names; each placement keeps the five fields the sets read
findings.test: tests/test_store_sets_decisions.py; the stage built alone in 160 seconds on the real store

findings.defect: An interrupt does nothing while a run swaps, and the guard only sent an interrupt
findings.scenario: the scheduler sent an interrupt when free disk fell under two gigabytes and the run went on for hours
findings.cause: the interpreter could not run its handler while it waited on swap
findings.fix: interrupt, terminate after thirty seconds, kill after thirty more; a swap limit before the disk fills

findings.defect: I called the scheduler's low-disk line a label when the guard had really fired
findings.scenario: the log said stopped: free disk under 2 GB and I told the owner it was only a label
findings.cause: I did not read the guard's code before saying so
findings.fix: corrected to the owner at once; the cause was the run's own swap filling the disk

measurements.name: set stages built alone on the real store
measurements.result: decisions, others, experiments, dclab_code, verified_code, routing, llm, then the tutor, the service files and the catalog all finished with no errors; the whole run in one process was stopped twice by the swap guard
limits: the whole conductor in one process is still not proven on this Mac
the llm stage still holds all its examples in memory and finished alone without trouble

outcome: The store is built stage by stage with no errors. The whole run in one process still cannot be shown to fit; the llm sets should stream each set to disk.
lessons: read the guard before explaining a log line
an interrupt is not a stop when a process swaps: escalate
a watcher whose own command line holds the search words matches itself
risks: a kill during a write could leave a half file; the store replaces files atomically
the next whole run may still be stopped by the swap limit
